name: murn
author: physics-agent (invented physics on ASCII pictures)
description: PRIVATE. Invented gravity on an ASCII scene. Clue is 'FOOTPRINT|n': FOOTPRINT is the ground row of a picture over the alphabet '#' (stone), 'o' (wood), '.' (air), 9-16 cells wide; n is the total number of stones the finished picture must contain. The answer is the whole picture, rows joined by newlines, ALL rows the same width, with its LAST row exactly equal to FOOTPRINT (spaces are read as air, leading/trailing blank lines are ignored). The invented law of support: a cell that is not on the ground is held only by the three cells directly beneath it (SW, S, SE); a stone needs EXACTLY two of them occupied, a piece of wood EXACTLY one. Nothing may stand on zero supports (no floating) and nothing may stand on three (over-braced -- so solid pyramids and solid slabs are illegal and structures come out lacy). Material does not matter for supporting, only for being supported. Intended discovery path: the bottom row of a demo is visibly the clue's footprint and the stone count is visibly n (one demo); the support law needs a second/third demo plus probes, because the natural priors ('rests on the block below', 'at least one support', 'at least two') all produce over-braced cells and score 0. Degenerate witnesses closed: the footprint alone (generate guarantees at least 3 stones must be added above the ground), the empty string and the clue itself (alphabet/bottom-row checks), a solid block or pyramid (the 'exactly' clauses), and wood-only towers (n counts stones). 65% of clues cannot be finished with a single extra row, so wood scaffolding must be built to reach the quota. solve() randomises height, stone placement and adds a decorative wood attic so demos never show a minimal witness.
